nom: KORRES Mineral Milk Fluid Sunscreen SPF 50

concerns.dehydration: One reviewer with dehydrated skin reports the product leaves skin hydrated and 'glass-skin nourished' with daily use.
concerns.oiliness: Multiple reviewers report it does not leave skin feeling oily or greasy and melts in without a heavy feel; no reports of increased oiliness.
concerns.spots: One reviewer reports it broke her out; no other reviewer mentions breakouts, so this appears to be an isolated reaction.

extraits.titre: Broke me out and doesnt blend
extraits.texte: This broke me out, and it also doesn't blend. It left white spots on your face!

Obsessed with this sunscreen/skincare POWERHOUSE! Feels like I'm actually taking care of my skin by protecting AND good skincare all packed into one. I use this in the mornings for my no makeup or minimal makeup looks and I swear it leaves my skin hydrated and glass-skin nourished! Many sunscreens break me out or leave me greasy (ew) but this one is wonderful, simple and cares for my skin. 10/10 for a dehydrated skin girlie like me

So happy this product finally launched in the US!! I have bought it abroad and love it so much. It doesn't leave your skin feeling oily and melts right into your skin without any white cast. 10/10 would recommend!!

extraits.titre: the only sunscreen I've ever liked
extraits.texte: I avoid wearing sunscreen daily because I hate how it feels. this is the first sunscreen i'm happy to put on daily - it blends in well and wears so well with makeup. it makes me feel hydrated and glowy. i also wore it on a boat day and it protects well!
I was lucky enough to get my hands on this product recently and I cannot say enough good things! It melts into the skin without feeling heavy or pore-clogging. Makes me excited for summer!
This is the best replacement I've been able to find for Tula's Mineral Magic. It's hydrating without looking or feeling greasy or sticky, and doesn't leave a white cast.

reserve: The reviews rarely state the reviewer's skin type explicitly, so segmentation by skin type is very limited and mostly inferable only from concerns like dehydration.
